title: Hip examination
stem: Cubicle 22. Mr Ho, 64, has had increasing right groin pain for 6 months, worse walking, and now struggles to put on his socks. Examine his hip and explain your findings.
notes:
Checked against NICE NG226 (Osteoarthritis, 2022) and standard hip examination.

Look (gait: antalgic or Trendelenburg; standing: Trendelenburg test for abductor weakness; scars, wasting, pelvic tilt, leg length — true (ASIS to medial malleolus) versus apparent (umbilicus to medial malleolus)), feel (greater trochanter tenderness for bursitis), move (flexion, extension, abduction, adduction, internal and external rotation — internal rotation is lost first in OA), special tests (Thomas test for fixed flexion deformity; FADIR/FABER). Examine the lumbar spine and the knee (referred pain), and neurovascular status.

OA is a clinical diagnosis in people 45 or over with activity-related joint pain and morning stiffness of 30 minutes or less (NICE); X-ray is not needed to diagnose it, but in the ED it helps exclude fracture or other pathology. Management: exercise, weight loss, analgesia, walking aids, and orthopaedic referral when symptoms affect quality of life despite treatment. Your notes list look (Trendelenburg, gait, leg length, Galeazzi), feel, move and Thomas test — matching.

steps.label: Examine the hip
steps.hint: Gait, Trendelenburg, leg lengths, feel, movements, Thomas test, spine and knee.

Look.t: Trendelenburg test standing on the right leg
Look.r: Pelvis drops on the left: positive on the right.

Look.t: Measure true and apparent leg lengths
Look.r: True lengths equal; apparent shortening on the right from pelvic tilt.
Look.mark: Measures true and apparent leg length

Move.t: Flexion and rotations with the hip at 90°
Move.r: Flexion 90°, internal rotation 5° and painful, external rotation 20°.
Move.mark: Tests rotations; finds loss of internal rotation

Move.r: Right thigh lifts off the couch: 15° fixed flexion deformity.

Complete.t: Examine the lumbar spine and knee; pulses and sensation
Complete.mark: Examines the joint above and below and neurovascular status

steps.ask: Thank you. Please present your findings.
steps.label: Present
steps.hint: Likely right hip OA; X-ray; conservative care; referral.

opts.t: Right hip osteoarthritis: groin pain, loss of internal rotation, fixed flexion deformity, positive Trendelenburg
Pelvis and hip X-ray to exclude other causes; analgesia, exercise, weight loss, walking stick in the left hand; orthopaedic referral
opts.mark: Management plan including stick in the opposite hand

opts.t: A stick in the right hand
opts.r: A stick is held in the opposite hand to offload the painful hip.

qs.a: Fixed flexion deformity of the hip
wrong: A true leg length discrepancy from the ASIS
A knee effusion on the patellar tap test

qs.q: Positive Trendelenburg on the right means…
qs.a: Pelvis drops on the left when standing on the right
wrong: The right knee buckles when standing on it
Pain in the right groin on weight-bearing
The left leg is short when measured from ASIS

qs.q: First movement lost in hip OA?
True leg length is measured from…

qs.a: Loss of joint space, osteophytes, sclerosis, cysts
wrong: Periosteal reaction and a sunburst pattern
Soap-bubble lucency in the femoral head
Periarticular erosions with osteopenia and joint-space loss

badge.name: Hip Check
badge.flavor: Internal rotation goes first. Stick in the other hand.

cards.q: Apparent leg length is measured from…
options: Greater trochanter to the lateral knee joint line
Hamstrings on the same side as the hip
Hip adductors on the opposite side
cards.why: Pelvis drops on the opposite side.

cards.q: NICE: OA can be diagnosed clinically in people aged…
options: Any age, but only once an X-ray confirms it

cards.q: Walking stick for right hip pain goes in…
cards.why: Reduces load on the painful hip.

options: Infants for developmental dysplasia of the hip
cards.why: Knee heights compared with hips flexed.
